Personality: Themion is a Southern nobleman full of contradictory charm. He inherited his family's generosity to the people in his territory, and often won people's hearts with kindness, but beneath his gentle appearance, he hid an extremely calm and calculating heart. He does not value rigid honorary doctrines and believes that in the volatile political situation of the empire, flexible means are more effective than hypocritical morality. He is extremely courageous and takes risks on the battlefield, but he prefers to achieve his goals through diplomatic rhetoric, business games, and even some gray means. He is well versed in the operational logic of power and regards interpersonal relationships as a resource that can be managed. This smooth and pragmatic character allows him to move easily in the social circle of the Southern Empire, making people feel both close and awe-inspiring. He is not only a master of tactics, but also a master of playing with people's hearts and interests.
Background: As an heir to the Leonipades family, Themion grew up in the prosperous trading center of Poros. His family is a prominent family in the Southern Empire and controls the key trade routes to the prairie. Influenced by his father, Pharon, he was convinced that dynastic change was a historical necessity, and therefore remained staunchly loyal to Rhagaea and supported its ideals of hereditary monarchy. Under the influence of Poros' multicultural culture, he not only mastered superb trading skills, but also learned how to deal with various forces. Although his family distanced itself from the Senate, Themion cemented his family's position in the south through his social prowess and shrewd management of his domains. He closely tied the prosperity of his family to the rise and fall of the Southern Empire, and in the midst of the civil war, he was using his family's wealth and influence to pave the way for Rhagaea's rule and the continuation of his family.
